themes.theme: State committed after generate/reroll is assembled ad hoc, per-field, from a mix of the pre-dispatch request and the post-dispatch resolved view — with no single reconciliation point. This drops rule rows that didn't resolve (rebuilt from view.constraints), lets the Advanced/export polish setting describe a pass that never ran (view.settings keeps the un-downgraded value), and forces three rounds of hand-tuned dispatch ordering just to keep seed/settings honest.
findingSummaries: handleReroll re-derives rule-editor rows from view.constraints/view.names via toNamedPairs, silently deleting any row that didn't resolve to an index pair (unmatched names, half-typed rows, duplicates) — the exact index-reconstruction the code's own comments forbid.

generate() downgrades an explicit polish:true to "auto" before dispatch, but pending.current.settings keeps the original un-downgraded value, so view.settings.polish (shown in the Advanced panel and written into the export file) describes a pass that never actually ran — the same class of bug as the seed-drift issue the surrounding comments were written to fix.

Reroll dispatch deliberately commits view.settings (not the locally-built request) with seed synthesized only for dispatch and synced back afterward; the three-round debate documented in the surrounding comment shows this ordering is fragile and easy to regress.
themes.remediation: Stop reconstructing committed state field-by-field from two different sources (the request vs. the resolved view). Delete the two divergent writes — the setConstraintRows(toNamedPairs(view.constraints, view.names)) call in handleReroll, and the separate un-downgraded polish value kept in pending.current.settings — so the only thing ever written back to App/hook state after a generate is the single settings object that was actually dispatched, and rows are left untouched unless the source is a full file import (the one place index-only data legitimately exists).

themes.theme: Documented extension seams for features the plan has committed to but not yet scheduled (F9 minimal-disruption recalc priors, a third GraphCanvas layout mode) have no caller today, so their real shape is still speculative.
findingSummaries: F9 (priors-based recalc) would require coordinated changes across GenerateRequest/GenerateOptions/ConstraintPair, useBuddyGraph's dispatch, and an undecided UI home in RosterModal — none of which currently know about 'the previous view's edges'.

GraphCanvas's LAYOUT_MODES/FIT_MODES/positionsFor seam is exhaustive and sound for its two existing cases (ring/force), but has only ever served one variant pair; the only candidate third case (focus/ego layout) is explicitly deferred with four unresolved hazards cataloged in app/CLAUDE.md.
themes.remediation: No code change now — the correct subtraction is to not build either seam ahead of a real caller (no speculative GenerateOptions fields, no generalized positionsFor signature) until F9 or focus/ego layout is actually scheduled.

themes.theme: A function or prop signature is looser or vaguer than what the implementation actually requires, leaving room for a future caller to violate a constraint the code never states in its type or name.
findingSummaries: neighborhood() performs a degree-capped walk (max 144 ops) but its name gives no hint of the bounded-degree assumption, only the JSDoc does.

GraphCanvas's route prop is typed optional (number[] | null | undefined) but buildHighlight needs null specifically; App.tsx coerces with route ?? null at its one call site today, but nothing stops a future caller from passing undefined straight through.
themes.remediation: Tighten the signature instead of documenting around it: make GraphCanvas's route prop required as `route: number[] | null` (drop the optional/undefined case) so the ?? null coercion collapses into the type itself and no caller can skip it; leave neighborhood's cap as the existing JSDoc rather than adding a second explanation.

themes.theme: An invariant that spans two code locations (a boundary-crossing assumption) is upheld by convention rather than being enforced at a single point, so the two sites can silently drift apart.
findingSummaries: toConstraints() normalizes pair order to required-then-prohibited regardless of input order; RosterModal's pre-flight check and the worker's check rely on this normalization matching, but the equivalence is implicit and undocumented at either call site.

PersonPanel documents its index parameter as requiring [0, view.names.length) but only App.tsx's caller enforces the range — PersonPanel itself has no guard, so reuse elsewhere would inherit an unenforced precondition.
themes.remediation: Remove the duplicate/split enforcement instead of documenting it: drop RosterModal's separate pre-flight ordering-dependent constraint check and rely solely on the worker's post-build validation (already the source of truth via report.refusals) as the one place order-equivalence matters; likewise drop the caller-side range guard in App.tsx and let PersonPanel's own eccentricity call be the sole enforcement point for its index precondition.

themes.theme: A confirmable keyboard/screen-reader action produces no perceivable feedback whenever the live-region text happens not to change — at a clamped boundary, or on an identical repeat within the auto-clear window — so the user cannot tell their press registered.
findingSummaries: The 'Buddies each' stepper clamps silently at BUDDY_MIN/MAX: the live-region text doesn't change and the +/- buttons carry no disabled state, unlike ConstraintsEditor's atCap pattern, so a keyboard/screen-reader user gets no signal they've hit the limit.

BuddyList's Copy button feedback lives entirely in the live-region text; pressing Copy again while the label still reads 'Copied' (within the 4s auto-clear window) sets identical text, so the region doesn't re-announce and a same-window re-press is silent.
themes.remediation: Eliminate the code path that lets a triggering action leave the live-region text unchanged: disable the +/- buttons at BUDDY_MIN/BUDDY_MAX (mirroring ConstraintsEditor's disabled={atCap}) so a no-op press can't happen at all, and clear the live region before rewriting it on every Copy press so identical successive messages can never survive untouched.

gating.invariant: For every code path other than import, the `NamedPair[]` committed to App's `constraintRows` is content-identical to the rows the user last submitted; equivalently, `toNamedPairs(view.constraints, view.names)` may only be assigned to `constraintRows` on the import path, and for all other paths `constraintRows` after the transition equals `constraintRows` before it.

gating.failure: Reproduced in /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/r-app/probe5.test.ts: n=80, k=12 (autoPolishEnabled(80,12,{constrained:false}) === false). The app dispatches options.polish="auto" and the core declines, so the graph is unpolished; the view/file keep settings.polish === true. The organizer's file therefore records a configuration that does not reproduce the graph beside it.
gating.remediation: Store the DISPATCHED options on the view rather than the requested ones: have `generate` write the downgraded `polish` into `pending.current.settings` so `view.settings` (and hence the Advanced panel, the export file, and the next reroll) is the configuration that actually produced the edges. If the user's raw choice must still be shown, keep it as a separate editor-side field rather than letting the view carry a value the graph does not satisfy.
gating.invariant: For every GraphView produced by generation, re-running the same builder with `view.settings` at `view.names.length` reproduces `view.edges` exactly — i.e. `view.settings` is always the option set that was dispatched, never a superseded request.

gating.theme: Function name does not convey its performance-critical bounded-degree assumption
gating.summary: neighborhood() performs a degree-capped walk (max 144 operations), not a general neighborhood computation, but the name does not indicate this constraint
gating.failure: A maintainer reading the function name and JSDoc might assume it computes unrestricted neighbors and be surprised by the degree cap or consider refactoring it to use Graph BFS (defeating the performance optimization). CLAUDE.md documents the exception but the code itself does not make the constraint obvious.
gating.remediation: Rename to `degreeCappedbNeighborhood()` or `boundedNeighborhood()`, or add a comment at line 24 clarifying: 'Limited to BUDDY_MAX degree per node for performance (O(k²) vs O(n+m))'. The JSDoc mentions the cap but the function signature does not hint at it.

gating.theme: Multiple review rounds tuning state-dispatch ordering in reroll path creates maintenance hazard
gating.summary: Reroll dispatch deliberately commits view.settings (not s) to state, with seed synthesized only for dispatch, then synced back from the resulting view. The comment (lines 237-250) documents three rounds of prior debate about this.
gating.failure: The logic is correct: (1) compute s with new seed, (2) commit view.settings to state, (3) dispatch with s, (4) sync view back. But someone reading only part of this logic or trying to 'simplify' by committing s directly would reintroduce the desync bug that motivated the current structure. New maintainers may not realize the three-part contract between handleReroll, setSettings, and the useEffect at line 124.
gating.remediation: Extract the dispatch-and-sync contract into a named helper function: `function rerollWithNewSeed(view: GraphView, settings: Settings): void { const s = {...}; setSettings(view.settings); bg.generate(view.names, s, ...). }` This would make the atomic operation and its invariants explicit. Or add an invariant test: after a successful reroll, verify that App.settings.seed equals view.settings.seed.

gating.theme: Constraint order is implicitly normalized across abstraction boundaries, creating a hidden invariant
gating.summary: toConstraints() normalizes ConstraintPair order to 'required-then-prohibited' regardless of input order. This normalization is implicit and lives in the middle of the constraint flow, so the equivalence between RosterModal's pre-check (using resolveNamedPairs order) and the worker's check (using joinPairs order) is not obvious.
gating.failure: If someone refactors toConstraints() to not split and re-order (e.g., to preserve input order for debugging), the pre-check and worker validation could diverge and produce different Constraints. The tests pass, but the implicit contract is not documented in the calling code.
gating.remediation: Add a comment at the toConstraints call site (constraints.ts line 93) and in RosterModal (around line 144): '// toConstraints normalizes to required-then-prohibited regardless of input order, so pre-flight and worker validation are equivalent'. Or move the normalization into splitPairs() and make it explicit in the return type.

gating.theme: a custom stepper's clamp-at-bound state has no accessible representation, so a keyboard/screen-reader user who presses past the limit gets no perceivable feedback that anything happened
gating.summary: The 'Buddies each' stepper (+/- buttons around a role="status" live-region span) is reachable and operable by keyboard, and the component's own comment (lines 28-34) explicitly reasons about announcing the new value after a press because a focus-retaining button gives no other feedback. But when settings.buddies is already at BUDDY_MAX (12) or BUDDY_MIN (2), setK() clamps the result back to the same value, so the live-region text does not change, the buttons carry no `disabled`/`aria-disabled`, and there is no boundary message anywhere (contrast ConstraintsEditor's 'Add a buddy rule', which both disables at MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS and has a `role="status"` note explaining why). A screen-reader user (or any keyboard user relying on the announced value) pressing '+' repeatedly at the ceiling hears nothing and has no way to distinguish 'my press didn't register' from 'I'm already at the limit'.
gating.failure: Render SettingsControls with settings.buddies = BUDDY_MAX (12). Press the '+' button (aria-label 'more buddies, currently 12') three times. The role="status" span's textContent stays "12" → "12" → "12" (no DOM mutation, so nothing is announced), and the button has no disabled/aria-disabled attribute at any point — verified with a scratch RTL test (.review-scratch/stepperBound.test.tsx) asserting the live region's textContent is byte-identical before and after three presses at the bound, and that the button carries neither `disabled` nor `aria-disabled`. Symmetric at BUDDY_MIN with the '-' button.
gating.remediation: Disable the '+' button (with `disabled` or `aria-disabled="true"`) once settings.buddies === BUDDY_MAX, and the '-' button at BUDDY_MIN — mirroring ConstraintsEditor's `disabled={atCap}` pattern — or, if the buttons must stay enabled, add a permanently-mounted boundary note (e.g. "That's the most buddies each person can have.") whose text changes precisely when the press was a no-op, so the live region's silence is never the only signal.
gating.invariant: For a bounded custom stepper, pressing the button in the direction of a bound that is already reached must either (a) mark that control disabled/aria-disabled, or (b) produce a DOM-text change in an accessible live region announcing the boundary — it must never be the case that the control remains fully enabled with no accessible-tree change on press.

gating.theme: identical successive live-region text is not re-announced, so a repeated confirmable action (Copy) gives no feedback on the second press within the auto-clear window
gating.summary: The 'Copy' button's only feedback is the `.sr-live` region's text ("Buddy list copied to the clipboard.") plus the button's own label flipping to "Copied". If the user presses Copy again while the label still reads "Copied" (within the 4s AUTO_CLEAR_MS window — realistic for a user unsure the first press registered, especially since clipboard writes are awaited and there is no other synchronous feedback), `setCopied(true)` is called again but the string is identical, so the live region's textContent does not change and nothing is (re-)announced. A screen-reader user gets confirmation on the first press only; a same-second re-press is silent.
gating.failure: Render BuddyList with a stubbed clipboard, click 'Copy', wait for the label to read 'Copied', then click it again immediately. Confirmed with a scratch test (.review-scratch/copyReannounce.test.tsx): the `.sr-live` region's textContent is identical before and after the second click, i.e. no DOM mutation occurs on the repeat press even though the action (a fresh clipboard write) did happen.
gating.remediation: Make the announcement distinguishable on a repeat within the window — e.g. append a monotonic counter or timestamp to an off-screen portion of the live-region text, or briefly clear the region to "" and re-set the message on every successful copy (matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this app for guaranteeing a live-region text change registers).
gating.invariant: Every user-triggered confirmation written into a live region must produce a DOM text change on each successful invocation of the action it confirms, even when consecutive invocations would otherwise render identical text.

confirmed.theme: Function name does not convey its performance-critical bounded-degree assumption
confirmed.summary: neighborhood() performs a degree-capped walk (max 144 operations), not a general neighborhood computation, but the name does not indicate this constraint
confirmed.failure: A maintainer reading the function name and JSDoc might assume it computes unrestricted neighbors and be surprised by the degree cap or consider refactoring it to use Graph BFS (defeating the performance optimization). CLAUDE.md documents the exception but the code itself does not make the constraint obvious.
confirmed.remediation: Rename to `degreeCappedbNeighborhood()` or `boundedNeighborhood()`, or add a comment at line 24 clarifying: 'Limited to BUDDY_MAX degree per node for performance (O(k²) vs O(n+m))'. The JSDoc mentions the cap but the function signature does not hint at it.

confirmed.theme: Multiple review rounds tuning state-dispatch ordering in reroll path creates maintenance hazard
confirmed.summary: Reroll dispatch deliberately commits view.settings (not s) to state, with seed synthesized only for dispatch, then synced back from the resulting view. The comment (lines 237-250) documents three rounds of prior debate about this.
confirmed.failure: The logic is correct: (1) compute s with new seed, (2) commit view.settings to state, (3) dispatch with s, (4) sync view back. But someone reading only part of this logic or trying to 'simplify' by committing s directly would reintroduce the desync bug that motivated the current structure. New maintainers may not realize the three-part contract between handleReroll, setSettings, and the useEffect at line 124.
confirmed.remediation: Extract the dispatch-and-sync contract into a named helper function: `function rerollWithNewSeed(view: GraphView, settings: Settings): void { const s = {...}; setSettings(view.settings); bg.generate(view.names, s, ...). }` This would make the atomic operation and its invariants explicit. Or add an invariant test: after a successful reroll, verify that App.settings.seed equals view.settings.seed.

confirmed.theme: Constraint order is implicitly normalized across abstraction boundaries, creating a hidden invariant
confirmed.summary: toConstraints() normalizes ConstraintPair order to 'required-then-prohibited' regardless of input order. This normalization is implicit and lives in the middle of the constraint flow, so the equivalence between RosterModal's pre-check (using resolveNamedPairs order) and the worker's check (using joinPairs order) is not obvious.
confirmed.failure: If someone refactors toConstraints() to not split and re-order (e.g., to preserve input order for debugging), the pre-check and worker validation could diverge and produce different Constraints. The tests pass, but the implicit contract is not documented in the calling code.
confirmed.remediation: Add a comment at the toConstraints call site (constraints.ts line 93) and in RosterModal (around line 144): '// toConstraints normalizes to required-then-prohibited regardless of input order, so pre-flight and worker validation are equivalent'. Or move the normalization into splitPairs() and make it explicit in the return type.

confirmed.theme: PersonPanel has precondition guard on the caller side only, increasing risk if component is reused
confirmed.summary: The index parameter is documented as a PRECONDITION (must be in range [0, view.names.length)) but the guard is enforced by the caller (App.tsx line 79-80), not by PersonPanel itself. The error is loud (eccentricity throws on out-of-range), so this is not a correctness bug in isolation.
confirmed.failure: If PersonPanel is ever used from another call site or if the caller's guard logic changes, the precondition could be violated silently for the range of indices where eccentricity doesn't throw (this is low probability but not zero). For maintainability, preconditions on component props should be validated at the component boundary.
confirmed.remediation: Add a guard inside PersonPanel before calling eccentricity: `if (index < 0 || index >= view.names.length) throw new Error('index out of range');`. This moves the contract from caller to component and makes it obvious in code that the precondition is non-negotiable.

confirmed.theme: a custom stepper's clamp-at-bound state has no accessible representation, so a keyboard/screen-reader user who presses past the limit gets no perceivable feedback that anything happened
confirmed.summary: The 'Buddies each' stepper (+/- buttons around a role="status" live-region span) is reachable and operable by keyboard, and the component's own comment (lines 28-34) explicitly reasons about announcing the new value after a press because a focus-retaining button gives no other feedback. But when settings.buddies is already at BUDDY_MAX (12) or BUDDY_MIN (2), setK() clamps the result back to the same value, so the live-region text does not change, the buttons carry no `disabled`/`aria-disabled`, and there is no boundary message anywhere (contrast ConstraintsEditor's 'Add a buddy rule', which both disables at MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS and has a `role="status"` note explaining why). A screen-reader user (or any keyboard user relying on the announced value) pressing '+' repeatedly at the ceiling hears nothing and has no way to distinguish 'my press didn't register' from 'I'm already at the limit'.
confirmed.failure: Render SettingsControls with settings.buddies = BUDDY_MAX (12). Press the '+' button (aria-label 'more buddies, currently 12') three times. The role="status" span's textContent stays "12" → "12" → "12" (no DOM mutation, so nothing is announced), and the button has no disabled/aria-disabled attribute at any point — verified with a scratch RTL test (.review-scratch/stepperBound.test.tsx) asserting the live region's textContent is byte-identical before and after three presses at the bound, and that the button carries neither `disabled` nor `aria-disabled`. Symmetric at BUDDY_MIN with the '-' button.
confirmed.remediation: Disable the '+' button (with `disabled` or `aria-disabled="true"`) once settings.buddies === BUDDY_MAX, and the '-' button at BUDDY_MIN — mirroring ConstraintsEditor's `disabled={atCap}` pattern — or, if the buttons must stay enabled, add a permanently-mounted boundary note (e.g. "That's the most buddies each person can have.") whose text changes precisely when the press was a no-op, so the live region's silence is never the only signal.
confirmed.invariant: For a bounded custom stepper, pressing the button in the direction of a bound that is already reached must either (a) mark that control disabled/aria-disabled, or (b) produce a DOM-text change in an accessible live region announcing the boundary — it must never be the case that the control remains fully enabled with no accessible-tree change on press.

confirmed.theme: identical successive live-region text is not re-announced, so a repeated confirmable action (Copy) gives no feedback on the second press within the auto-clear window
confirmed.summary: The 'Copy' button's only feedback is the `.sr-live` region's text ("Buddy list copied to the clipboard.") plus the button's own label flipping to "Copied". If the user presses Copy again while the label still reads "Copied" (within the 4s AUTO_CLEAR_MS window — realistic for a user unsure the first press registered, especially since clipboard writes are awaited and there is no other synchronous feedback), `setCopied(true)` is called again but the string is identical, so the live region's textContent does not change and nothing is (re-)announced. A screen-reader user gets confirmation on the first press only; a same-second re-press is silent.
confirmed.failure: Render BuddyList with a stubbed clipboard, click 'Copy', wait for the label to read 'Copied', then click it again immediately. Confirmed with a scratch test (.review-scratch/copyReannounce.test.tsx): the `.sr-live` region's textContent is identical before and after the second click, i.e. no DOM mutation occurs on the repeat press even though the action (a fresh clipboard write) did happen.
confirmed.remediation: Make the announcement distinguishable on a repeat within the window — e.g. append a monotonic counter or timestamp to an off-screen portion of the live-region text, or briefly clear the region to "" and re-set the message on every successful copy (matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this app for guaranteeing a live-region text change registers).
confirmed.invariant: Every user-triggered confirmation written into a live region must produce a DOM text change on each successful invocation of the action it confirms, even when consecutive invocations would otherwise render identical text.

plausible.theme: GraphCanvas route prop is optional but buildHighlight requires null, not undefined
plausible.summary: route prop is declared as `route?: number[] | null;` (optional, can be undefined). At line 208 it is converted to null with `route ?? null` before passing to buildHighlight. If a caller forgets this coercion and passes undefined, buildHighlight receives undefined and may not highlight the route correctly.
plausible.failure: buildHighlight checks `route !== null` at line 37 (highlight.ts). If route is undefined, this check is truthy, and the function treats it as an active route when it should not. The route would be used as `route.length` or array indexing elsewhere, potentially causing silent logic errors.
plausible.remediation: Change the route prop type to `route?: (number[] | null);` with explicit default at call site, OR change buildHighlight to accept `route?: number[] | null` and handle undefined. Most simply: in GraphCanvas, declare route prop as `route: number[] | null;` (required, never optional) and let the caller (App.tsx line 334) handle the coercion.
